Independent C++ finite generator/checker (independent_checks.cpp) re-enumerated every 8/3-free prefix through n=30, checked all insertion extensions, and matched all 30 populations and the two exact witnesses.
correctness.rationale: Every exponent-at-least-8/3 factor with least period p has a period-p threshold subfactor of length ceil(8p/3). Prefix generation rejecting newly created forbidden suffixes is exhaustive: a newly invalid word must have a forbidden suffix. Independently compiled and ran a separate C++ period-threshold generator for lengths 1..30. It reproduced all 30 populations (ending 34,880;48,020;66,102), found no extremal word below 30, and exactly the two stated length-30 words. Both words were independently checked under every one-letter insertion. Exhaustion proves this finite minimum, but neither larger-length classification nor higher-threshold existence.
residual_risks: Enumeration proves only the n<=30 claim, not an infinite existence theorem or an upper threshold beyond 8/3.
